title: Qcqs integral rational scalar extension preserves finite models and Tor intervals
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and a finite subextension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $\Lambda=\underline E$, the condensed ring of continuous functions to normed $E$, or $\Lambda=\Omega^{\mathrm{fin}}$, whose sections on a profinite set are continuous functions to $\Omega$ with image in one finite subextension [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. Put $\mathcal F=\{E\}$ in the first case and let $\mathcal F$ be all finite subextensions of $\Omega$ in the second. For $F\in\mathcal F$ write $A_F=\mathcal O_F$ with its norm topology. For each scheme $T$, use the pulled-back condensed coefficient rings $\Lambda_T,F_T,A_{F,T}$ on the small pro-étale site, module objects, and ordinary uncompleted unbounded derived categories [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull, def-weil-size-convention]. Constructibility means finite constant scalar models on a finite constructible locally closed stratification; $D_{\mathrm{ctf}}$ means bounded constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. A lisse module is pro-étale locally free of finite rank. A scheme is qcqs when it is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism].

Let $T$ be qcqs and $F\in\mathcal F$. The coefficient map $A_{F,T}\to\Lambda_T$ is flat. The derived scalar-extension functor $T_{F,T}=\Lambda_T\otimes^L_{A_{F,T}}-$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars] is canonically exact termwise scalar extension and is triangulated. For every integer $q$ and every $J\in D(A_{F,T})$, it has the natural derived cohomology identification $H^q(T_{F,T}J)\cong\Lambda_T\otimes_{A_{F,T}}H^q(J)$. If $J\in D_{\mathrm{ctf}}(T,A_F)$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$, then $T_{F,T}J\in D_{\mathrm{ctf}}(T,\Lambda)$ with Tor amplitude in the same interval. On every stratum on which $H^q(J)$ has finite constant scalar models, $H^q(T_{F,T}J)$ has pro-étale locally finite free models. These assertions concern module objects with their actual relative tensors, equivalently the section-ring-sheaf realization; they impose no derived completeness or Noetherianity.

proof.text: Integral rationalization has exact scalar extension by integralScalarExtension_exact. For the closure compose with the exact finite-subfield inclusion. coefficientMap_comp and Mod.extendScalarsComp identify this composite with the required extension. Both functors preserve finite colimits as left adjoints.

Use the canonical leftDerivedFunctorIsoMapDerivedCategory and invertible leftDerivedFunctorCounit for an exact functor. Transport the triangulated structure along this comparison, with exactly the shift structure integralCTFShift. leftDerivedFunctorHomologyFunctorIso gives the natural cohomology comparison; bounded_mapDerivedCategory_obj gives boundedness.

A right exact additive functor carrying the regular module to the regular module preserves finite presentations: map the cokernel of a map between finite powers, use mapBiproduct and PreservesCokernel.iso, then conjugate the presenting map by those isomorphisms. Apply this with scalar extension and Mod.regularExtensionIso. Coefficient extension commutes with upperStar by CondensedRing.pullIso. It commutes with pullback from the point by uniqueness of left adjoints: the right adjoints agree by mapModComapIso, comapComp and naturality of the adjunction unit. Hence each specified finite constant local model extends on its original cover; in Lean these elementary assemblies are finitePresentation_map, pointExtensionIso and localModel_extension.

Over each target coefficient ring, every finite scalar presentation is free of finite rank. Reuse lattice_scalar_free, finite_point_scalars and closure_point_scalars from QcqsConstructibleIntegralLatticeTree (only these proved Gaussian-elimination helpers, not its lattice-existence theorem). The point section ring is the field F or PadicAlgCl; the finite scalar matrix has a basis of its cokernel, including rank zero. models_free_cover from FiniteConstantLocalModel transports this to a free module on the given cover. The cohomology comparison and pullIso therefore give free models on each original stratum, and finite constant models prove constructibility using the same stratification.

Scalar extension preserves flat module objects by Mod.extendScalars_preservesFlat. Apply the already proved source-library theorem DerivedCategory.torAmplitudeIn_mapDerivedCategory_obj to the exact functor: it maps a flat model supported in [a,b] to a flat model with the same support. Its proof uses the bounded flat model characterization of the actual derived Tor predicate, so no monoidal structure on the scalar-extension functor or section-ring-sheaf realization is required. Transport the interval along leftDerivedFunctorIsoMapDerivedCategory. Combine with boundedness and constructibility from the preceding steps to obtain the required D_ctf assertion and the same specified interval.
